ahara: Meat-soup of domestic, aquatic and marshy animals

purvaroopa: Liking for comfort in lying, sitting and sleeping
Smearing sensation in heart, eyes, tongue and ears
Excessive growth of hairs and nails
Burning sensation in hands and feet
roopa: Kaphaja (10 types): urine watery, like sugarcane juice, viscous, with solid precipitate, white, with semen, cold, with slow impulse, saliva-like, with gravels
Pittaja (6 types): urine like alkali, black, blue, yellow like haldi, light red like manjistha, deep red
Vataja (4 types): urine with majja, with ojas, with vasa, with laska
diseases.sadhyata: Kaphaja and pittaja without premonitory symptoms are maintainable; vatika prameha and congenital / hereditary cases are incurable

vihara: Suppression of natural urges particularly vomiting
Physical exercise and intense heat after eating excessively
Use of cold water after sun exposure, exertion and fear

purvaroopa: Excessive pain in wounds with quick origin and delayed healing
roopa: Kapala kustha: black and reddish, rough, coarse, thin, exceedingly painful
Audumbara kustha: burning sensation, itching, pain, redness, brown skin hairs, like ripe udumbara fruit
Mandala kustha: white, red, stable, extensive, unctuous, raised patches joined together
Rsyajihva kustha: rough, red margins, internally blackish, painful, like antelope tongue
Pundarika kustha: whitish, red margins, raised, like lotus petals, burning sensation
Sidhma kustha: white, coppery, thin, dust-like powder on rubbing, like bottle gourd flowers, mostly in chest
Kakanaka kustha: gunja seed colour, does not suppurate, exceedingly painful, tridosaja
Ekakustha: no perspiration, extensive, like fish-scales
Carmakhya: thick-skinned like elephant
Kitibha: blackish, rough like corn, coarse
Vipadika: tearing of hands and feet with excessive pain
Alasaka: itching, red glandular pimples
Dadru: raised patch, itching, redness, pimples
Carmadala: red, itching, eruptions, pain, flakes, tenderness
Pama: white, reddish, blackish pimples with excessive itching
Visphota: white and reddish, thin-walled eruptions
Sataru: red or blackish, burning sensation, pain, multiple boils
Vicarcika: itching, blackish pimples with excessive discharge
bheda: Mahakustha (7 major): Kapala, Audumbara, Mandala, Rsyajihva, Pundarika, Sidhma, Kakanaka
Kshudrakustha (11 minor): Ekakustha, Carmakhya, Kitibha, Vipadika, Alasaka, Dadru, Carmadala, Pama, Visphota, Sataru, Vicarcika
diseases.sadhyata: Kapala and mandala are hardly curable; kakanaka is incurable; tridosaja forms are difficult; single dosa and vata-kapha forms are easier

roopa: Daruna: red spot, morbidity in blood
Aruna: coppery spot, morbidity in flesh
Switra: white spot, morbidity in fat
diseases.sadhyata: Incurable if: undemarcated, extensive, with red hairs, arisen many years ago. Curable if: no red hairs, thin, pale, not old, raised in middle

ahara: Various foods and drinks taken irregularly
vihara: Battle, weight-lifting, travelling on foot, leaping, jumping

purvaroopa: Wasting of strength and flesh despite meals
Longing for women, wine and meat
Often falling of flies, insects, hairs in food and drink
roopa: Cough
Distress in shoulders
Derangement of voice (hoarseness)
Fever
Pain in sides
Headache
Haemoptysis (blood in sputum)
Excretion of sputum
Dyspnoea
Diarrhoea
Anorexia
diseases.sadhyata: Curable if strong; incurable if emaciated and weak with all symptoms

ahara: Uncooked, pungent, sour, burning and hot edibles (pittaja)
agantuja: Insult to gods, sages, gandharvas, pisacas, yaksas and forefathers

roopa: Vataja: inopportune laughing, smiling, dancing, singing, speaking, weeping; roughness, emaciation, reddish complexion; aggravation after digestion
Pittaja: intolerance, agitation, nakedness, terrorising, excessive movements, heat, wrath, desire for shade, cold food; yellowish lustre
Kaphaja: slow speech and movements, anorexia, liking for women and loneliness, excessive sleep, vomiting, salivation, aggravation on taking meals, whiteness of nails
Sannipataja: all above characters combined; incurable
Exogenous (agantuja): superhuman speech, colour, power, movements; irregular time of aggravation
bheda: Agantuja unmada (8 types: from gods, sages, forefathers, gandharvas, yaksas, brahmaraksasas, raksasas, pisacas)
diseases.sadhyata: Sannipataja and those striking others violently are incurable; others are treatable

manasa: Affliction of mind with rajas and tamas

roopa: Departure of memory
Unconsciousness
Loathsome appearance
Derangement of intellect and mind
Falls
Twitching in tongue, eyes and eyebrows
Excessive salivation
Convulsions in hands and feet
Vatika: trembling, biting teeth, froth, excessive respiration, sees things as rough reddish black
Paittika: yellow froth, limbs face and eyes yellow, thirst, heat, sees environment as on fire
Kaphaja: white froth, cold, horripilated, heavy, sees things white, recovers after long period
Sannipataja: all symptoms combined
diseases.sadhyata: Sannipataja, wasted person and old are incurable; others treatable with difficulty; chronic in nature
